item.title: Tensor Degenerations for Matrix Multiplication
item.description: arXiv:2610.13971v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let ${\mathbb K}$ be an arbitrary field. We study tensor degenerations for square matrix multiplication over the field ${\mathbb K}$, and mainly prove for any integer $n\ge5$ the uniform dyadic estimate \[ \underline{\mathrm R}_{\mathbb K}({\mathsf M}_{2^n}) \le 2^{2n+1}\] which implies that $\omega(\mathbb K)\le 2+1/n$, where the border rank $\underline{\mathrm R}_{\mathbb K}(T)$ is the least $r$ for which the scalar extension of $T$ to an algebraic closure of $\mathbb K$ lies in the Zariski closure of the tensors of rank at most $r$, and $\omega(\mathbb K)$ is the matrix multiplication exponent over the field ${\mathbb K}$. This improves the current best record $\omega(\mathbb K)<2.371177$ greatly, and answers affirmatively the long-standing open question whether the value $\omega({\mathbb K})$ is exactly $2$. The implementation disclosure and appendices in this paper give fixed source maps, interpolation data, terminal incidence ledgers, and deterministic check counts for independent reconstruction.
item.dc:creator: Zhi-Wei Sun

item.title: Associativity of discretized triangular norms
item.description: arXiv:2610.14072v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we mainly investigate when the binary operation $T^{[n]}:[0, 1]^2\rightarrow [0, 1]$ satisfies the associative law and thus becomes a triangular norm where \begin{equation*} T^{[n]}(x,y)=\left\{\begin{array}{ll} f_{n}(T(f_{n}(x),f_{n}(y))), &\text{if}\,\, (x,y)\in{[0,1)^{2}}, \\ \min\{x,y\}, &\text{otherwise,} \end{array}\right. \end{equation*} $f_{n}:[0,1]\rightarrow\left\{0, \frac{1}{n}, \frac{2}{n}, \dots, \frac{n-1}{n}, 1\right\}$ given by $f_{n}(x)=\frac{1}{n}{\lfloor nx \rfloor}$ with $n$ a positive integer and $T:[0, 1]^2\rightarrow [0, 1]$ is a triangular norm. We present some sufficient conditions for $T^{[n]}$ to be triangular norms, and for $T^{[n]}$ to be never associative when $T$ is strictly monotonic.
item.dc:creator: Di Zhang, Xue-ping Wang

item.title: How long is a game of Uno? A counting law for large hands and the Wild Draw Four hoard
item.description: arXiv:2610.14076v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the length of one round of Uno under the official rules, for N players who each start with M cards. The fastest possible round takes at least M turns with two players and at least 2M-1 turns with three or more, and both bounds are attained for small M. An exact search over random deals shows that real deals rarely allow them. Under the official rules a round has no maximum length. Under forced play the probability that a round lasts more than t turns decays exponentially in t at a rate that does not depend on M. Our main result concerns very large hands. If every card a player ever holds is eventually played, a round lasts (27/19)NM turns to first order, and the constant depends only on the composition of the deck. The official rule that a Wild Draw Four may only be played by a player who holds no card of the current colour breaks this law. Every large hand hoards Wild Draw Fours, M/23 of them per player, and the round ends with a dumping endgame. For an even number of players this gives (53/46)NM turns. For an odd number of players the dumping cannot alternate round the table, and the endgame settles into a seating pattern whose turn rate we compute numerically. Simulations with up to 32,000 cards per hand support these limits. Finally we solve a small strategy game: with two players the Nash equilibrium over a family of 48 strategies is a single pure strategy that wins 62.8% of rounds against uniformly random play.
item.dc:creator: Pragyaan Gaur

item.title: Zeros and Their Distribution for Leonardo Polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.14080v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the zeros of Leonardo polynomials and their distribution in the complex plane. We show that the structure of the zeros differs between even and odd degrees. For even degrees, all zeros are simple and purely imaginary, with imaginary parts lying in \((-2,2)\). For odd degrees, there is exactly one positive real zero, whereas no negative real or purely imaginary zeros occur. We obtain two-sided bounds for the unique positive real zero, prove that it decreases strictly to zero as the degree increases through odd values, and determine its asymptotic behavior. Using the relation between Leonardo and Fibonacci polynomials together with a complex trigonometric parametrization, we transform the zero equation into a family of fixed-point problems. Suitable invariant disks are constructed, and the corresponding mappings are shown to be contractions. This yields a constructive description of the complete zero set, proves the simplicity of all zeros, and provides geometrically convergent iterations for their numerical approximation. The method also provides explicit control over the approximation error. Finally, we establish a degree-dependent vertical strip containing all zeros and show that its width tends to zero as the degree increases. Consequently, the zeros become uniformly concentrated near the imaginary axis. Numerical examples illustrate the convergence of the proposed method, the associated error estimates, and the resulting zero distributions.
item.dc:creator: Muhammet Karag\"oz, Nihal \"Ozg\"ur

item.title: Signed Quantities and Quadrilaterals: Geometry without Cases
item.description: arXiv:2610.14452v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ordinary angles and unsigned areas discard orientation, and much of the case analysis in plane geometry is the price of that loss. Signed quantities (directed angles, oriented areas and directed distances) keep the signs and so let one argument serve for every configuration. We illustrate this with results that hold uniformly for convex, concave and crossed quadrilaterals: the diagonal area formula, an identity expressing one diagonal in terms of the sides and the other diagonal, a test for a pair of parallel sides, a theorem on equidiagonal quadrilaterals (such a quadrilateral has a pair of equal opposite sides if and only if it has a pair of parallel opposite sides), and a single ratio of directed distances that decides whether the vertices lie on an ellipse, only on hyperbolas, or on a circle.
item.dc:creator: George-Rubin Thomas

item.title: Primes and irreducible polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2302.14849v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In 2002, M.Ram Murty showed that if p is a prime with k-adic expansion :$p = \sum_{i = 0}^n a_i k^i$ , then the polynomial $f(x) = \sum_{i = 0}^n a_ix^i$ is irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$.When $k = 10$ , it's a result of A.Cohn. I think this kind of polynomials is really interesting and worse to speak more. So I plan to find more conclusions about this kind of polynomials. In the first section of this article, author proves a stronger version of this theorem that if we multiply prime $p$ by a factor $t$ that is smaller than $k$ ,the conclusion also holds. In the second section, author further consider larger multiplier $t$ ,and gives a technique to control one of the factors of the polynomial.
item.dc:creator: Boyang Zhao

item.title: A Survey on Lawvere's Fixed-Point Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2503.13536v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Lawvere's fixed-point theorem organizes self-reference around a representation hypothesis and a diagonal calculation. This survey develops its set-theoretic, finite-product, and cartesian closed formulations while distinguishing representation on points from equality of whole morphisms. Detailed applications include Cantor's theorem, arithmetic diagonalization, a truth-schema obstruction, an incompleteness consequence with explicit assumptions, the halting problem, and Kleene's recursion theorem. A powerset dcpo supplies a nontrivial positive representation of continuous maps and illustrates the difference between fixed-point existence, a uniform operator, and a least fixed point. Further sections compare parameterized recursion and trace, substructural and relational generalizations, constructive witness data, and topological variants. Throughout, the relevant maps, equality relations, and additional hypotheses are kept explicit. Worked examples use finite tables, Boolean equations, numerical function codes, factorial approximations, and self-output programs. The survey is intended for readers beginning category theory who wish to understand both the common diagonal mechanism and the work required in its applications.
item.dc:creator: Joaquim Reizi Higuchi

item.title: A Ramanujan Pell K3 Surface and Cube Representations
item.description: arXiv:2607.11925v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A negative Pell equation produces positive integers with $a_n^3+b_n^3+c_n^3=561N_n^3+(-1)^{n+1}$. We classify all positive solutions satisfying the natural linear constraints of the construction and prove an exact pairwise coprimality law, with exceptional factor $137$ in one class modulo $68$. The associated sextic $K=(1-13u+26u^2)^3+(6+182u^2)^3$ defines an elliptic K3 surface with six type-IV fibres. Its genus-four cubic cover has a geometrically simple Prym threefold; exact good-reduction arithmetic establishes simplicity over every finite extension of the residue field. We determine the full geometric Mordell-Weil group, the integral Neron-Severi and transcendental lattices, and the arithmetic Picard lattice over $\mathbb{Q}$, which is $U\oplus\langle-4\rangle^{\oplus4}$. Every two-cube representation by rational functions over $\mathbb{Q}$ is obtained from a multiple of one section, with numerator degrees $2m^2$ and denominator degree $2m^2-2$. Polynomial rigidity follows without a degree assumption. Along the specified Pell orbit all specialized points are nontorsion, their heights are $\frac{4}{3}|n|\log(8+\sqrt{65})+O(1)$, and infinitely many rational cubic-twist classes occur. We also identify the local zeta function at $19$ and the generic rank and rank-jump criterion for the corresponding two-parameter base-change family.
item.dc:creator: K. Srinivasa Raghava

item.title: Walsh eta-units at squarefree level-integral structure and Fricke values
item.description: arXiv:2607.11926v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For squarefree $M>1$, we determine the quotient of the principal cuspidal lattice of $X_0(M)$ by the sum of its primitive Atkin-Lehner character sublattices. Its invariant factors are explicit at every level. The quotient is a 2-group, and with $k\ge3$ prime divisors its exponent is exactly $2^{k-2}$, the sharp universal power expressing every modular unit, modulo constants, through primitive sign units. We construct mixed generators and operator actions and relate the quotient to cuspidal class numbers and integral Eisenstein periods. At the Fricke point, singleton exponent sums determine the prime factors of every normalized unit value; the remaining factor is an algebraic unit. When the quadratic order has class group of exponent at most two, Kronecker's limit formula expresses the even sign values as explicit rational powers of real quadratic fundamental units. The Fricke-fixed coefficient identity for $1/\pi$ leads to a strictly monotone equation with rigorous truncation certificates. For reciprocal sign products we prove a colored-partition asymptotic and a congruence modulo 5. The classical eta representation and Kronecker-Pell results are explicitly identified as inputs.
item.dc:creator: K. Srinivasa Raghava

item.title: Admissible $qx+1$ Sequences, Semiconvergents, and Rational Catalan Numbers
item.description: arXiv:2609.22303v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For an odd integer $q\geq3$, let $a_q(r)$ count finite words in $\{q/2,1/2\}$ containing exactly $r$ factors $q/2$, with every proper prefix product greater than $1$ and total product less than $1$. For $q=3,5,7$, these are OEIS A100982, A174795, and A174796. The increasing-sequence representation yields a range identity and, for A100982, an exact recurrence valid at every order. Using the classical cycle lemma, we prove the natural lower and upper binomial bounds and characterize equality. The equality orders are precisely the strict lower and upper one-sided best-approximation denominators to $\log_2q$, equivalently the convergent and semiconvergent denominators and the record approaches of $q^r$ to powers of $2$. At every nontrivial equality order, the admissible words are in bijection with rational Dyck paths and their number is a rational Catalan number. We also prove monotonicity in $q$, determine the exponential growth constants, and describe the exact normalized oscillation.
item.dc:creator: Mike Winkler

item.title: P is not equal to NP
item.description: arXiv:math/0702261v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we prove that P is not equal to NP. The proof is based on the Boolean Satisfiability problem(SAT). For any algorithm to solve SAT instances, we prove that there is an exponential lower bound in computation complexity, so that we have P is not equal to NP.
item.dc:creator: Yanyou Qiao
